Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

{"visible_record": {"initial_information_actually_supplied": "A man first seen at age 41 has recurrent painful oropharyngeal ulceration causing dysphagia, followed by ulcers of the eyelids, tongue dorsum, lip mucosa and penis. Eyelid inflammation caused scarring and ocular surface complications; it is not described as uveitis. Over several years he also has periodic fever, lower-leg swelling/erythema, sicca symptoms, abdominal pain and diarrhoea.
Treatment and investigation have been complicated by infections, including severe C. difficile colitis after clindamycin for a suspected oropharyngeal infection, bowel perforation and resections. Multiple oral, skin and gastrointestinal specimens show non-specific changes without demonstrated granulomas or vasculitis; direct immunofluorescence is negative. No haematological malignancy was established by marrow, flow, protein, imaging and panel workup. Hilar lymphadenopathy was not found, and broad autoimmune serology was not explanatory.
No genetic result, final syndrome label or later response to immunomodulation is given. Negative or non-specific biopsies should be described precisely rather than turned into a universal exclusion rule.", "original_task": "Audience: a clinician. Use 200–280 words in English. Synthesise the ulcer and multisystem pattern, compare broad inflammatory/autoinflammatory, infectious and other relevant explanations and state what specialist clarification is needed. Distinguish underlying disease from treatment-associated complications. Do not prescribe a new immunosuppressive regimen or require a rare syndrome name unsupported by the disclosed evidence. Use only the supplied information at this decision point. Separate observed facts, hypotheses and proposed actions. Do not invent measurements, negative findings, treatment responses or probabilities. Do not give a drug dose or a fixed treatment regimen. Give concise clinical justifications, not a private reasoning trace.", "audience": "Clinician", "task_mode": "written", "actual_dialogue_and_public_notes": [], "closing_public_assessment_note": {}, "final_answer_unchanged": "Observed facts: 41‑year‑old man with recurrent painful oropharyngeal ulceration causing dysphagia, subsequent ulcers of eyelids, tongue dorsum, lip mucosa and penis. Eyelid inflammation led to scarring and ocular surface complications; not uveitis. Over years periodic fever, lower‑leg swelling/erythema, sicca symptoms, abdominal pain and diarrhoea. Severe C. difficile colitis after clindamycin, bowel perforation and resections. Multiple oral, skin and GI specimens show non‑specific changes without granulomas or vasculitis; direct immunofluorescence negative. Extensive haematological work‑up negative for malignancy. No hilar lymphadenopathy. Broad autoimmune serology non‑explanatory. No genetic result, final syndrome label or later immunomodulation response provided.

Hypotheses: 1) Autoinflammatory syndrome (e.g., Behçet‑like, PFAPA, NLRP3‑associated) given recurrent mucosal ulcers, fever, skin and ocular involvement. 2) Complex immune dysregulation with secondary infection susceptibility. 3) Infectious mimic (e.g., chronic viral, mycobacterial) not yet excluded. 4) Paraneoplastic or occult lymphoma despite negative work‑up. 5) Treatment‑related complications: clindamycin‑induced C. difficile colitis, surgical sequelae.

Proposed actions: Refer to multidisciplinary immunology/rheumatology clinic for systematic autoinflammatory work‑up including cytokine panels, NLRP3 sequencing, and repeat mucosal biopsy with immunohistochemistry. Ophthalmology review for ocular surface disease. Infectious disease consultation to rule out occult infection before escalation of immunosuppression. Gastroenterology follow‑up for post‑surgical bowel status. An essential requirement is one whose omission materially compromises the assessment or decision required by the task. Its relevance must be justified by the presentation available at that point, not by hindsight from a hidden result or later outcome. The key should specify acceptable requests, alternatives, timing, and how the information can be obtained within the task constraints.", "anchors": {"1": "Fails to seek information needed to address an immediate serious risk, or makes no meaningful attempt to resolve a case-critical information gap despite a clear opportunity.", "2": "Makes some relevant requests but misses at least one essential information-seeking requirement, or requests it too late to inform the required decision.", "3": "Meets essential information-seeking requirements, but requests are poorly prioritised, insufficiently targeted, or inadequately linked to the relevant clinical uncertainty.", "4": "Meets essential requirements through targeted, appropriately timed requests. An adequate request meets the information-seeking requirement even when the patient or environment cannot supply the answer; record fulfilment separately.
